# Iteration 2 {.unnumbered}

In Iteration 1, you moved quickly through the complete machine-learning workflow and built your first classification, regression, and clustering models.

In Iteration 2, you go through the first stages of the workflow again, but this time **in greater depth**: you build your own dataset from the raw HOPV files, and you train your first models on it.

The work is still structured: notebooks and resources will guide you through the main steps. However, you will begin making more decisions yourself and applying concepts introduced in the self-study material.

## Business Understanding

Before going deeper into the data, develop enough domain understanding to reason about what you are modelling.

Read:

* [SMILES: A Simplified Chemical Language](https://www.daylight.com/dayhtml/doc/theory/theory.smiles.html) (Daylight Theory Manual)

Your goal is **not to master chemistry**. Focus on understanding what SMILES strings represent and how they describe molecular structure.

## Data Understanding

Explore the HOPV data, identify the input and target variables, investigate data quality, and examine important distributions and relationships.

Complete **in order**:

1. [Understanding HOPV Stability](01_understanding_stability_data.ipynb)
2. [Understanding HOMO/LUMO Data](02_understanding_homolumo_data.ipynb)

## Data Preparation

Turn the raw molecular data into data suitable for machine-learning models.

Complete:

* [Data Preparation](03_data_preparation.ipynb)

## Baseline

Train your Iteration 1 classification, regression and clustering models again, in the same way, on your new dataset. These scores are the baseline that you improve in Iteration 3.

Complete:

* [Baseline](04_baseline.ipynb)

## Keep iterating

Although the notebooks provide a structured path, the machine-learning workflow is not strictly linear.

What you discover in the baseline may give you a reason to return to the data, change its preparation, investigate a new feature, or revisit your understanding of the problem.

In [Iteration 3](../iteration-3/index.qmd), you improve the models with cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning, take a closer look at the clusters, and make your first Kaggle submission.
